theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (-0.67%) and Utilities (-1.27%) led the market today, while Technology (-6.99%) and Consumer Discretionary (-4.14%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -4.42% versus -1.30% for defensives and -2.64% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -3.12% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -5.13%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -4.52%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 61.56% to 26.77, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.81% to $4,116.30, crude oil was little changed at $90.25, and bitcoin slipped 5.60% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
